faqs.a: It depends on height and sex. As a rough guide, a lean fit man carries about 70-80% of his weight as lean mass; a fit woman about 65-75%. Athletes sit higher.
faqs.q: What is a good lean body mass?

faqs.a: No. Lean mass includes muscle plus bone, water, organs, and everything that is not fat. Skeletal muscle is only part of it.
faqs.q: Is lean body mass the same as muscle mass?

faqs.a: Progressive resistance training plus enough protein (about 1.6-2.2 g per kg of body weight) and a small calorie surplus. Beginners gain roughly 0.25-0.5 kg of muscle per month.
faqs.q: How do I increase lean body mass?

faqs.a: The Boer formula assumes an average build. If you carry more fat than average for your height and weight, your real lean mass is lower than the estimate.
faqs.q: Why is my lean mass lower than the Boer estimate?

faqs.a: Yes - it is the better base. Protein at about 2 g per kg of lean mass and lean-mass-based calorie formulas beat weight-based rules for muscular or overweight people.
faqs.q: Should I use lean mass for calorie targets?

faqs.a: Monthly, under the same conditions: morning, before food. Daily readings bounce with water and food.

lean-body-mass-calculator.formula:
From body fat:
LBM = weight x (1 - bodyFat% / 100)

Boer estimate:
Men: LBM = 0.407 x W(kg) + 0.267 x H(cm) - 19.2
Women: LBM = 0.252 x W(kg) + 0.473 x H(cm) - 48.3

Example: man, 80 kg, 175 cm
= 0.407 x 80 + 0.267 x 175 - 19.2 = 32.56 + 46.73 - 19.2 = 60.1 kg.
howTo: If you know your body-fat %, choose 'From body fat' and enter weight and the percentage.
If you do not, choose 'Estimate (Boer)' and enter sex, height, and weight.
Your lean mass, fat mass, and body-fat % appear instantly.
Track monthly: rising lean mass at a steady weight means your training works.
For calorie and protein targets, base them on lean mass, not total weight.
keyFacts: Lean body mass = weight minus fat mass. It includes muscle, bone, water, and organs.
From body fat %: LBM = weight x (1 - bodyFat / 100).
Boer formula (men): 0.407 x weight(kg) + 0.267 x height(cm) - 19.2.
Boer formula (women): 0.252 x weight(kg) + 0.473 x height(cm) - 48.3.
Healthy body-fat ranges: roughly 10-20% for men, 18-28% for women.
Two people at the same weight can have very different lean mass - that is why BMI alone misleads athletes.

lean-body-mass-calculator.quickAnswer: Lean body mass is everything except fat: weight x (1 - body-fat / 100). At 80 kg and 20% body fat, your lean mass is 64 kg and your fat mass is 16 kg. Without a body-fat reading, the Boer formula estimates lean mass from height, weight, and sex - about 60.1 kg for an 80 kg, 175 cm man.
lean-body-mass-calculator.tagline: Find your lean mass from weight and body fat, or estimate it with the Boer formula.
lean-body-mass-calculator.workedExample:
You weigh 80 kg with 20% body fat:
1. Convert % to a fraction: 20 / 100 = 0.20.
2. Lean fraction: 1 - 0.20 = 0.80.
3. LBM = 80 x 0.80 = 64 kg.
4. Fat mass = 80 - 64 = 16 kg.

Boer estimate for an 80 kg, 175 cm man:
1. 0.407 x 80 = 32.56; 0.267 x 175 = 46.73.
2. Sum minus 19.2: 79.29 - 19.2 = 60.1 kg lean mass.
3. Implied body fat: (80 - 60.1) / 80 = 24.9%.
